claims.text: Localized thermal gradients govern the magnetocaloric response of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale films or nanoribbons under low applied fields.
Localized thermal gradients govern magnetic hysteresis in these films or nanoribbons.
Thermal gradients generate associated local strain fields.
The local strain fields induce heterogeneous nucleation of magneto-structural transitions.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons exhibit local thermal gradients.
The as-deposited material exhibits spatially inhomogeneous magneto-structural transition behavior.
An ultrathin AlN overlayer provides enhanced local heat dissipation because of its high thermal conductivity.
Enhanced heat dissipation from the overlayer reduces nanoscale thermal gradients and localized overheating.
Reducing localized overheating reduces related strain and local phase heterogeneity.
Nanoscale phase heterogeneity can govern magnetic hysteresis through its effect on magnetic or structural behavior.
Reduced thermal and strain heterogeneity produces more uniform nucleation and propagation of magneto-structural transitions.
More uniform magneto-structural transition behavior reduces magnetic hysteresis.
Coated samples will have a smaller hysteresis-loop width than uncoated as-deposited controls.
Coated samples will exhibit a larger magnetocaloric response, including a larger adiabatic temperature change, than uncoated controls.
The uncoated baseline has significant hysteresis and suboptimal magnetocaloric performance because of local thermal gradients.
The proposed mechanism is active at applied magnetic fields on the order of tens of millitesla.
The proposed mechanism is active below 1 Hz, where heat transfer is rate limiting.
Film morphology and deposition conditions can alter nanoscale heat transfer and local strain fields.
